Plan: Parting Shot now to drop the opposing Incineroar's Attack and Sp. Atk, then bring in Garchomp (Mega available). Earthquake is 2x on Incineroar. Watch their Life Orb Incineroar, Aegislash, Gholdengo, Corviknight, Toxapex and Dragapult, and track their speed. Dragapult is the fast threat.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing my options here: my Incineroar is at 180/202 with lowered attack, facing the opponent's Incineroar at 90% health holding a Life Orb, also with lowered attack after Fake Out. Flare Blitz would be resisted by their Fire typing, so that's only neutral effectiveness against their Dark typing overall, making it a less appealing choice.

Switching Garchomp in is tempting since it's at full health and Fake Out is already spent, though the opponent's Intimidate would trigger again and drop Garchomp's attack. I'm also considering Parting Shot, which would further lower the opponent's Incineroar to -2 attack while letting me pivot into Garchomp or Kingambit safely without re-triggering Intimidate on my own side.

Kingambit's Dark-type moves are resisted by Incineroar's Dark typing, and Iron Head is just neutral against Fire, so it's not ideal either. Garchomp's Earthquake hits Incineroar for a solid 2x since Ground is super effective against Fire, making it the strongest offensive option despite the Intimidate drop and Life Orb chip damage it'd take coming in.

Parting Shot is the better play: it drops the opposing Incineroar's Attack and Special Attack while letting me pivot Garchomp in for free, keeping my Incineroar healthy. Garchomp will still eat an Intimidate drop on the switch, but Earthquake next turn should still be strong given the debuffs I've applied.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I'm weighing whether to send in Incineroar or Kingambit against their Incineroar at 90% health with Life Orb, Will-O-Wisp, and Fake Out—Kingambit's Steel typing leaves it vulnerable to Flare Blitz, so I need to think through the matchup carefully.

Kingambit's own moves against this Incineroar aren't great either—Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, and Sucker Punch all end up resisted since Incineroar's Dark typing blunts Dark moves and its Fire typing handles Steel decently. Supreme Overlord only gives Kingambit a modest boost here since just one ally (Garchomp) has fainted so far.

Comparing the mirror matchup, Incineroar vs Incineroar is tanky on both sides since Flare Blitz is only neutral-resisted at 0.5x, so I'm weighing whether to keep our Incineroar in (using Parting Shot to cripple their offense) versus switching to Kingambit, who'd take a scary 2x hit from Flare Blitz given its Fire weakness.

Since Garchomp fainted, the only legal choice now is a switch, and Incineroar seems like the safer pick—it can either trade blows or use Parting Shot to shift momentum while avoiding Kingambit's Fire weakness exposure.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Let me correct myself: only Garchomp fainted on our side, so Supreme Overlord should only be boosting by 10%, not the higher amount I noted earlier. Meanwhile the opposing Incineroar is at 80% HP, holding Life Orb, with its attack dropped by two stages.

Checking the matchups: Kingambit's Dark moves like Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch only hit Incineroar for 0.5x since it resists Dark, and Iron Head is similarly weak against Fire/Dark. On the flip side, Incineroar's Fire-type attacks like Flare Blitz hit Kingambit for double damage due to its Steel typing, though the -2 Atk drop should blunt that significantly given Kingambit's solid Def and large HP pool. I'm weighing whether to set up a Swords Dance here since Incineroar's offensive threat is weakened, or to press the attack directly.

Their Crunch does little since Atk is down, but Flare Blitz still hits hard at roughly double. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave lands around 59 per hit, needing three to take down Incineroar's 152 HP, though Swords Dance first would bump that to roughly 118 per hit for a two-hit kill — risky though, since a Flare Blitz near 125 damage threatens Kingambit's 188 HP.

Incineroar is faster anyway at 72+ Speed versus Kingambit's 70, so it acts first regardless. Given the opponent's low damage output overall, I'll commit to Swords Dance now and attack next turn.

Since Incineroar is Fire/Dark, Kowtow Cleave being Dark-type would only be resisted by itself, so I'm weighing whether the massive +4 boost still makes it a strong attack despite the burn and the type resistance.

So Incineroar survives at around 150 HP, not a KO, especially factoring Life Orb recoil considerations. Checking other options, Sucker Punch fails if Incineroar isn't attacking, and I'm double-checking Steel-type coverage against Fire/Dark since Steel resists Fire but hits Dark neutrally, not super effectively as I'd assumed.

Comparing Iron Head to Kowtow Clause, both land at 0.5x effectiveness, but Kowtow Cleave wins out with higher base power, STAB, Black Glasses boost, and guaranteed accuracy, plus Kingambit's lower speed doesn't matter since Kowtow never misses — so I'll go with Kowtow Cleave, assuming Incineroar just keeps using Protect again.
